```{r}
library(tidyverse)

```



===============================
# CHARGEMENT DES DONNÉES
===============================
```{r}
base_dir <- "c:/Users/sebpi/Documents/Travail/S7/DataScience"

features_path <- file.path(base_dir, "cleaned_data2/features_extracted_combined.csv")
target_path   <- file.path(base_dir, "cleaned_data/data_Y.csv")

X <- read.csv(features_path)
X

Y <- read.csv(target_path)
Y

# Harmonisation du nom de colonne
if ("sc" %in% colnames(Y)) {
  colnames(Y)[colnames(Y) == "sc"] <- "scenario_id"
}

# Fusion
data <- inner_join(X, Y, by = "scenario_id")
data
```
# ===============================
# PRÉPARATION X / y
# ===============================
```{r}
target_col <- "SMax"

X <- data %>%
  select(-scenario_id, -all_of(target_col))

y <- data[[target_col]]
```

# ===============================
# TRAIN / TEST SPLIT
# ===============================

```{r}
train_index <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)

X_train <- X[train_index, ]
X_test  <- X[-train_index, ]

y_train <- y[train_index]
y_test  <- y[-train_index]
```

# ===============================
# VISUALISATION AVANT SCALING
# ===============================

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2,3))
for (col in colnames(X_train)[1:min(5, ncol(X_train))]) {
  plot(X_train[[col]], y_train,
       xlab = col,
       ylab = target_col,
       main = paste("Unscaled:", col),
       pch = 16, col = rgb(0,0,0,0.5))
}
par(mfrow = c(1,1))
```


# ===============================
# SCALING (centrage-réduction)
# ===============================

```{r}
scaler <- preProcess(X_train, method = c("center", "scale"))

X_train_scaled <- predict(scaler, X_train)
X_test_scaled  <- predict(scaler, X_test)
X_full_scaled  <- predict(scaler, X)
```


# ===============================
# VISUALISATION APRÈS SCALING
# ===============================

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2,3))
for (col in colnames(X_train_scaled)[1:min(5, ncol(X_train_scaled))]) {
  plot(X_train_scaled[[col]], y_train,
       xlab = col,
       ylab = target_col,
       main = paste("Scaled:", col),
       pch = 16, col = rgb(0,0,1,0.5))
}
par(mfrow = c(1,1))
```

# ===============================
# MATRICE DE CORRÉLATION
# ===============================

```{r}
cor_mat <- cor(data %>% select(-scenario_id))
corrplot(cor_mat, method = "color", tl.cex = 0.6, na.label = " ", na.label.col = "white")
```

# ===============================
# LASSO CV
# ===============================

```{r}
{
set.seed(42)
lasso_cv <- cv.glmnet(
  x = as.matrix(X_train_scaled),
  y = y_train,
  alpha = 1,
  nfolds = 5,
  standardize = FALSE,
  keep = TRUE
)
}

best_lambda <- lasso_cv$lambda.min
best_lambda
```


# ===============================
# PERFORMANCE TEST
# ===============================
```{r}
y_pred_test <- predict(lasso_cv, s = best_lambda, newx = as.matrix(X_test_scaled))

r2 <- cor(y_test, y_pred_test)^2
rmse <- sqrt(mean((y_test - y_pred_test)^2))

r2
rmse
```


# ===============================
# COURBE MSE (CV)
# ===============================

```{r}
{
  # Récupérer les MSE pour chaque fold
  # cv.glmnet stocke les MSE dans un format différent de Python
  # On doit recalculer les MSE pour chaque fold à partir des prédictions
  lambda_seq <- lasso_cv$lambda
  
  # lasso_cv$fit.preval contient les prédictions pour chaque observation et chaque lambda
  # Dimensions: [n_observations x n_lambdas]
  # On doit calculer le MSE pour chaque fold
  
  # Récupérer les folds
  foldid <- lasso_cv$foldid
  n_folds <- max(foldid)
  n_lambdas <- length(lambda_seq)
  
  # Matrice pour stocker les MSE de chaque fold
  mse_folds <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_folds, ncol = n_lambdas)
  
  # Calculer MSE pour chaque fold et chaque lambda
  for (fold in 1:n_folds) {
    fold_idx <- which(foldid == fold)
    for (j in 1:n_lambdas) {
      pred <- lasso_cv$fit.preval[fold_idx, j]
      actual <- y_train[fold_idx]
      mse_folds[fold, j] <- mean((actual - pred)^2)
    }
  }
  
  # Créer le plot avec échelle log sur x (comme Python semilogx)
  plot(lambda_seq, lasso_cv$cvm, type = "n", log = "x", 
       xlab = "Alpha", ylab = "Mean Square Error",
       main = "Lasso MSE Path (5-fold CV)",
       ylim = range(c(mse_folds, lasso_cv$cvm), na.rm = TRUE))
  
  # Ajouter les lignes pour chaque fold (pointillés comme Python)
  for(i in 1:n_folds) {
    lines(lambda_seq, mse_folds[i,], col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.3), lty = 1)
  }
  
  # Ajouter la moyenne (ligne noire épaisse)
  lines(lambda_seq, lasso_cv$cvm, lwd = 2, col = "black")
  
  # Ajouter légende
  legend("topright", 
         legend = c("Average across the folds", paste0("Best alpha: ", round(best_lambda, 4))),
         col = c("black", "black"), 
         lty = c(1, 2), 
         lwd = c(2, 1),
         bty = "n")
  
  # Ajouter la ligne verticale du meilleur lambda
  abline(v = best_lambda, lty = 2, lwd = 1, col = "black")
}
```


# ===============================
# CHEMIN DES COEFFICIENTS
# ===============================

```{r, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}
lasso_path <- glmnet(
  x = as.matrix(X_train_scaled),
  y = y_train,
  alpha = 1,
  standardize = FALSE
)
{
  # Extraire les coefficients (beta est une matrice sparse)
  # Dimensions: [n_features x n_lambdas]
  coefs <- as.matrix(lasso_path$beta)
  alphas <- lasso_path$lambda
  
  # Générer une palette de couleurs pour mieux distinguer les features
  n_features <- nrow(coefs)
  colors <- rainbow(n_features, alpha = 0.6)
  
  # Configurer les marges pour un meilleur rendu
  par(mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
  
  # Créer le plot avec échelle log sur x (comme Python semilogx)
  plot(alphas, rep(0, length(alphas)), type = "n", log = "x",
       xlab = "Alpha", ylab = "Weights",
       main = "Lasso coefficients as a function of alpha",
       ylim = range(coefs),
       las = 1,  # Labels horizontaux sur l'axe Y
       cex.lab = 1.2,  # Taille des labels
       cex.main = 1.3)  # Taille du titre
  
  # Ajouter une grille pour faciliter la lecture
  grid(col = "gray90", lty = 1)
  
  # Tracer chaque coefficient avec des couleurs différentes
  for(i in 1:nrow(coefs)) {
    lines(alphas, coefs[i, ], col = colors[i], lwd = 1.5)
  }
  
  # Ajouter une ligne horizontale à y=0 pour référence
  abline(h = 0, col = "gray50", lty = 3, lwd = 1)
  
  # Ajouter la ligne verticale pour le meilleur lambda
  abline(v = best_lambda, col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2)
  
  # Ajouter légende avec fond blanc semi-transparent
  legend("topright", 
         legend = paste0("Best alpha: ", round(best_lambda, 4)), 
         col = "red", lty = 2, lwd = 2, 
         bg = "white", box.col = "gray80")
  
  # Remettre les marges par défaut
  par(mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2) + 0.1)
}

```


# ===============================
# OBSERVED VS PREDICTED (FULL DATASET)
# ===============================

```{r}
y_pred_full <- predict(lasso_cv, s = best_lambda, newx = as.matrix(X_full_scaled))
{
plot(y, y_pred_full,
     xlab = "Observed",
     ylab = "Predicted",
     main = "Observed vs Predicted (Lasso)",
     pch = 16, col = rgb(0,0,0,0.5))
abline(0, 1, col = "red", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
}
```

# ===============================
# FEATURES SÉLECTIONNÉES
# ===============================

```{r}
coef_lasso <- coef(lasso_cv, s = best_lambda)
coef_df <- data.frame(
  feature = rownames(coef_lasso),
  coefficient = as.numeric(coef_lasso)
) %>%
  filter(coefficient != 0, feature != "(Intercept)") %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(coefficient)))

cat("\nNumber of selected features:", nrow(coef_df), "\n")
cat("\nTop 5 coefficients:\n")
print(head(coef_df, 5))
```
